dwigraha.note: Two grahas occupying one sign, and what the verse says of the native. Read from N. Chidambaram Iyer's 1885 translation; Mantreswara gives the same twenty-one readings at Phaladeepika ch. 18 vv. 1 to 5. The chapter closes by saying that three or more together are read as the pairs they contain, which is what one rule a pair does of itself.

inRasi.note: A graha in a sign, and what the chapter says of the native. Read from R. Santhanam's translation of Kalyana Varma's Saravali, one chapter to a graha, the signs in order from Aries. The chapters add readings for the same graha under each other graha's aspect, and ch. 23 v. 88 makes the whole of them wait on the strength of the sign, its lord and the graha; neither is here, the kernel having no strength measure.

inBhava.note: A graha in a bhava, and what the verse says of the native. Read from R. Santhanam's translation of Kalyana Varma's Saravali, the houses in order from the ascendant. risingPart.note: The part of a sign that rises, and what the chapter says of the native. Read from R. Santhanam's translation of Kalyana Varma's Saravali, the signs in order from Aries and the parts in order from the beginning of each sign. Ch. 49 v. 25, ch. 50 v. 37 and ch. 51 v. 1 make these effects mature in full only where the sign, its lord, or the stronger of the navamsa lagna's lord and the Moon's navamsa dispositor is strong, which the kernel cannot measure; ch. 51 v. 110 carries the sign readings over to the dwadasamsas and the rest to the saptamsas, which is not built; the second decanates of Gemini and of Cancer are printed with one reading between them in the translation read, and both ship as printed.
